author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the readable page and the machine-readable list, can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. The narrowing is asked for with the request; no page control offers it.
acceptance_criteria: Both vet list surfaces accept an optional specialty value on the request, named specialty: /vets.html?specialty=<name> and /vets?specialty=<name>.
Given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, only those veterinarians are listed on the page and returned in the machine-readable list.
The specialty name is matched whole and letter case is disregarded; text that is only part of a specialty name matches no veterinarian.
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the normal page or machine-readable document successfully, with no veterinarian listed.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as if none had been named, as an empty owner search does, and the whole directory is returned.
With no specialty named, both surfaces behave exactly as they do today.
A specialty named with leading or trailing spaces is read as the name without them.
Paging through a narrowed page stays inside the narrowed list, and the paging links carry the named specialty.
The new behavior is covered by tests on both surfaces, including the no-match, blank, and case-difference cases.
non_goals: Any page control for choosing a specialty: no form, dropdown, or link. A visible control may be requested later.
Free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits: NG-9 stays in force for that.
Narrowing on more than one specialty at once.
Narrowing any other list in the system.
Removing or reshaping the machine-readable list beyond adding the narrowing.
notes: NG-9 is narrowed by ADR docs/adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md. REQ-VET-004 reinstates the machine-readable list as a supported surface, superseding the withdrawn REQ-VET-002; REQ-VET-002 is not reused. REQ-VET-004 needs no code work of its own, so this is the only slice. No prd-autofix records existed to audit. The index table in docs/adr/README.md still needs a row for the new ADR; that file is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter lands entirely inside the existing vet feature package and needs no new type. VetController keeps its two routes and gains an optional specialty parameter on each; VetRepository gains two narrowed finders alongside the two whole-directory ones. The blank-and-strip handling copies OwnerController.processFindForm, and the paged narrowed finder copies OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith. What is genuinely new is the cache boundary: every vet read is cached today under an unbounded JCache cache, and a finder keyed by request text cannot join it. That decision is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-07-uncached-filtered-vet-queries.md and summarized in docs/system-design.md#veterinarian-directory-routes, a new subsection under Contracts naming both routes and the parameter.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty request parameter; the paged model gains the specialty so the template can rebuild its links
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same parameter and needs a collection-returning narrowed finder, not the paged one
VetRepository gains two finders traversing Vet.specialties to Specialty.name; neither carries @Cacheable
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty through Thymeleaf link parameters
No change to Vet, Specialty, Vets, CacheConfiguration, the schemas, or the seed data

patterns.description: null-or-blank request value read as the broadest search, and stripped before use; copy the blank and strip handling only
Spring Data derived finder returning Page<T> for a paged, filtered list
the pagination block this template mirrors; its __${...}__ link form is the one part not to copy for the specialty

risks.risk: The implementer annotates the narrowed finders @Cacheable for symmetry with the two existing methods, putting caller-supplied text into an unbounded cache key space
risks.mitigation: docs/adr/2026-08-07-uncached-filtered-vet-queries.md decides against it; the narrowed finders stay uncached and the unfiltered ones keep their annotation unchanged

risks.risk: The specialty is spliced into the pagination link with Thymeleaf's __${...}__ preprocessing, as the existing links build the page number; preprocessing re-parses the substituted text as expression source, so request text becomes template code
risks.mitigation: build the links with the link-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=...)}, which URL-encodes the value; a test asserting a link for a specialty containing a quote or brace pins it

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching is left to column collation, repeating the PostgreSQL divergence recorded in docs/system-design.md#known-defects for owner search
risks.mitigation: fold case in the query itself, through the derived IgnoreCase keyword or an explicit lower() in JPQL; the H2 test suite cannot observe the divergence, so the mechanism is the guarantee

risks.risk: OwnerController.processFindForm rejects an empty result with a field error and redirects when exactly one row matches; copying it wholesale breaks two acceptance criteria
risks.mitigation: the narrowed directory always renders the list page with HTTP 200, empty or not, and never redirects on a single match

risks.risk: Paging over the vet-to-specialty join returns duplicate rows or a wrong total if a vet joins more than one matching specialty row
risks.mitigation: prefer a distinct derived finder and assert the total element count in the paging test, not only the page contents

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so nothing to audit. Both follow-ups the product-requirements-expert flagged are done: docs/adr/README.md gained the index row for the non-goal ADR, and docs/system-design.md#contracts gained a Veterinarian directory routes subsection naming both routes and the parameter. Three further durable-memory writes this slice required: the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less is removed, since REQ-VET-004 reinstates it; the vet Contracts rows now cite REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, and Vets is no longer an em-dash row; a Threat Model row records the reflected specialty value in the pagination links. Open Question 5 gained one sentence: the already-cached page query is keyed by a caller-supplied page number, so the unbounded key space predates this slice. That observation is not this slice's to fix. Vocabulary is settled in docs/ubiquitous-language.md: Veterinarian in prose, vet in code and page text, Specialty for the held field, and Vets only as a code symbol.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived finders findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and (String) in VetRepository. Both are derived-query bound parameters; no JPQL, no native query, no string concatenation anywhere in the diff. Matches the SQL-injection row of the Threat Model.

Template-expression injection (triage risk 2) verified independently, not taken on trust: vetList.html builds every one of the five paging links with the link-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}. Thymeleaf URL-encodes query-parameter values in a link expression and th:href output-escapes the resulting attribute, so a hostile value never re-enters the expression parser. Swept the whole templates/ tree for the preprocessing form (grep -F '__$'): the surviving __${...}__ occurrences are in fragments/inputField.html, fragments/selectField.html, fragments/layout.html, owners/ownerDetails.html and owners/ownersList.html, and each substitutes a template-literal field name, a hardcoded menu link, an entity identifier, or a computed page integer — none takes request-supplied text. The diff introduces no new preprocessing. VetControllerTests:162-164 pins the encoding with a specialty of radio"logy${1} rendering as specialty=radio%22logy$%7B1%7D, so the mitigation is regression-guarded, and VetControllerTests:176 pins that an unnarrowed request emits no specialty parameter at all.

XSS: no th:utext, no th:inline, and no [(...)] unescaped-output syntax exists anywhere under src/main/resources/templates/. The reflected specialty appears only inside th:href link parameters and the th:with narrowed boolean; it is never written into element text or an unescaped attribute. The link path is the fixed literal /vets.html, so no scheme or host is attacker-controlled and no open-redirect surface is added.

Cache key space (triage risk 1) verified independently: VetRepository:73-85 carries @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable on either narrowed finder, while the two whole-directory finders keep @Cacheable("vets") unchanged. Caller-supplied text therefore never becomes a key in the unbounded, eviction-free vets cache declared by CacheConfiguration. The Javadoc on both methods states the prohibition and cites the ADR, so the constraint survives a later edit by a reader who has only the file.

Input handling: VetController.namedSpecialty treats null and blank as naming no specialty and strips surrounding whitespace, so the unnarrowed path is byte-identical to the pre-change behaviour. page stays a primitive int, so a non-numeric value is rejected by binding rather than reaching the repository. No new binder configuration and no new mass-assignment surface — the diff adds two read-only GET routes and no write path.

Secrets: swept the production diff for credential-shaped names (token, password, secret, key, credential) — no hits. The change adds no configuration, no logging of the request value, and no new outbound connection or external service.

Supply chain: build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties and gradle/ are all unmodified (git status clean for those paths), so the change introduces no new dependency, no version bump, and no new transitive surface. Nothing in this slice widens the CVE exposure of the existing Spring Boot 4.1.0 tree.

Documentation matches the code: the new Threat Model row in docs/system-design.md describes the reflected specialty value and the link-parameter mitigation accurately, and the two ADRs record the cache decision the repository actually implements.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: prd.md REQ-VET-003 states 'given text that is only part of a specialty's name, when either form is asked for it, then no veterinarian matches.' Every other two-form acceptance criterion (held specialty, unheld specialty, blank specialty, case-insensitive match) got a dedicated test for both the paged Page<Vet> finder and the Collection findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) finder used by /vets. The partial-name-does-not-match criterion only got the paged-finder test (ClinicServiceTests.theVetDirectoryShouldNotMatchPartOfASpecialtyName, line 225); the Collection overload used by the machine-readable /vets endpoint has no test proving a partial name fails to match. The two overloads are independently-derived Spring Data queries, so a divergence in the second is not caught by the first.
findings.fix: Add theMachineReadableVetListShouldNotMatchPartOfASpecialtyName to ClinicServiceTests, mirroring theVetDirectoryShouldNotMatchPartOfASpecialtyName but calling vets.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("radio") (no Pageable) and asserting the Collection is empty.

findings.description: Local variable `Page<Vet> vets = this.vets.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("radio", pageable);` shadows the class field `this.vets` (the VetRepository). It happens to work because the local is always referenced without `this.`, but it defeats a reader's ability to tell field from local at a glance, and an accidental `this.vets` reference later in the method would silently resolve to the field instead of failing to compile.
findings.fix: Rename the local variable, e.g. `Page<Vet> matches = this.vets.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("radio", pageable); assertThat(matches).isEmpty();`

approved_aspects: Mocking policy honored: VetControllerTests mocks only VetRepository behind MockMvc (the sanctioned web-transport boundary), ClinicServiceTests exercises the real H2-backed repository end to end — no internal collaborator is mocked.

All nine REQ-VET-003 Done-when bullets have at least one dedicated test per form except the partial-match gap noted above: held-specialty match, case-insensitive match, blank-specialty passthrough, unheld-specialty empty-200 result, no-specialty passthrough, and narrowed pagination-link preservation are each covered for both /vets.html and /vets.

Reflected-value injection risk (ADR-called-out template-expression risk) is directly pinned: theNarrowedVetDirectoryShouldEncodeTheSpecialtyInPagingLinks asserts both the URL-encoded form is present and the raw quote-and-brace payload is absent from the rendered page.

Duplicate-row-per-join risk is covered at the real-query level: theNarrowedVetDirectoryShouldCountEachVeterinarianOnce exercises a vet holding two matching specialties (Douglas: dentistry+surgery seed data) and asserts totalElements is not inflated by the join.
All new test names follow the project's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school from testing-principles.md, a marked improvement over the pre-existing suite's method-name style in the same files.

Blank/whitespace-only specialty is verified as a true no-op via verify(vets, never()).findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(...), not just by an equivalent-output assertion, so the test would fail if a future change accidentally queried on blank text.
./gradlew test --tests VetControllerTests --tests ClinicServiceTests passes cleanly against the current build.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet feature package: two controller routes, two added repository finders, one template, plus tests. No sensitive paths, no schema or seed change, no shared type touched. The unnarrowed path stays byte-equivalent to today's, and the five rewritten paging links are pinned by a test asserting the old URL still renders when no specialty is named.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk and found nothing the description would not predict. namedSpecialty maps null and blank to null before stripping, so both surfaces delegate to the unchanged findAll when no specialty is named. The narrowed finders are derived queries with bound parameters; the whole-directory finders keep @Cacheable while the narrowed ones deliberately do not. The template rewrite is behaviour-preserving and keeps request text out of the preprocessing form.

test_adequacy.note: Tests are real (H2-backed repository tests plus MockMvc) and the encoding and no-parameter regressions are genuinely pinned, but two of the change's own claims are untested. theNarrowedVetDirectoryShouldCountEachVeterinarianOnce would pass with Distinct removed: Douglas holds surgery once, so the seed data cannot produce a duplicate row, and the comment claiming otherwise is wrong. The paging-stays-narrowed criterion is proven only against a mocked repository with a hand-built PageImpl; every integration-level narrowed query passes Pageable.unpaged(), so the derived query's real paging over the eager Vet.specialties join never runs against a database.

reviewer_hedging.note: Both second-pass approvals carry empty findings lists. The first pass's two changes_requested verdicts were all autofix-tagged, applied verbatim, and re-approved without residual caveats; the two bar_clause flags (tested-as-spec, legible-cold) were closed by the fix rather than argued down. Security-reviewer's absence from the fix pass is the risk-proportional plan scoping a test-and-docs delta, not silence.

scope_deviation.note: The slice reached past its URL contract into product decisions. It narrowed non-goal NG-9 (ADR-recorded, deliberate) and, with no ADR and zero consultations in the log, reversed the 2026-07-31 withdrawal of the machine-readable route by minting REQ-VET-004, deleting the Known Defects row saying that route remains pending removal, and marking the reinstatement confirmed 2026-08-07. The PRD's own new open question concedes the surface is supported again without a named consumer, which was the stated reason it was withdrawn.

rationale: The code is clean and preserves behaviour where it should. Read two things before merging: the dedup test proves nothing, since the seed data cannot produce a duplicate row, and the slice un-withdrew the /vets endpoint and rewrote a non-goal with no consultation on record.
